independent_variables.name: DiscIR_t
independent_variables.definition: Monthly discretionary information-risk factor-mimicking return. Each month, firms are independently ranked into quintiles using their most recent DiscAQ; the factor is average monthly excess return for the top two quintiles minus that for the bottom two. Fiscal-year-t DiscAQ scores are used to form portfolios for the 12-month period beginning in fiscal year t+1. Returns are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles before portfolio formation. DiscAQ is the Eq. (6) residual, based on AQ from Eq. (5); AQ is the time-series standard deviation of Eq. (5) residuals over years t−4 through t.
independent_variables.formula: Winsorize underlying firm returns at the 1st and 99th percentiles before forming quintile portfolios; the factor is the top-two-quintile mean monthly excess return on firms ranked by the most recent metric minus the bottom-two-quintile mean monthly excess return.

evidence.quote: DiscIR and InnateIR are the discretionary and innate information risk factors calculated using the DiscAQ and InnateAQ metrics.
Firms are independently ranked each month into quintiles based on their most recent AQ, DiscAQ, and InnateAQ values.
The information risk factor mimicking returns for AQ, DiscAQ, and InnateAQ are each equal to the difference between the monthly excess returns of the top two quintiles and bottom two quintiles.
fiscal-t metrics are used in twelve-month portfolios starting fiscal t+1.
We winsorize returns at the 1st and 99th percentiles before we form portfolios in order to reduce the effect of outliers.
The residual, l^i,t, from Eq. 6 is the estimate of the discretionary component of firm i’s accrual quality in year t, DiscAQi,t = l^i,t.

independent_variables.name: DiscIR_t
independent_variables.definition: Monthly discretionary information-risk factor-mimicking return. Each month, firms are independently ranked into quintiles using their most recent DiscAQ; the factor is average monthly excess return for the top two quintiles minus that for the bottom two. Fiscal-year-t DiscAQ scores are used to form portfolios for the 12-month period beginning in fiscal year t+1. Returns are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles before portfolio formation. DiscAQ is the Eq. (6) residual, based on AQ from Eq. (5); AQ is the time-series standard deviation of Eq. (5) residuals over years t−4 through t.
independent_variables.formula: Winsorize underlying firm returns at the 1st and 99th percentiles before forming quintile portfolios; the factor is the top-two-quintile mean monthly excess return on firms ranked by the most recent metric minus the bottom-two-quintile mean monthly excess return.

evidence.quote: DiscIR and InnateIR are the discretionary and innate information risk factors calculated using the DiscAQ and InnateAQ metrics.
Firms are independently ranked each month into quintiles based on their most recent AQ, DiscAQ, and InnateAQ values.
The information risk factor mimicking returns for AQ, DiscAQ, and InnateAQ are each equal to the difference between the monthly excess returns of the top two quintiles and bottom two quintiles.
fiscal-t metrics are used in twelve-month portfolios starting fiscal t+1.
We winsorize returns at the 1st and 99th percentiles before we form portfolios in order to reduce the effect of outliers.
The residual, l^i,t, from Eq. 6 is the estimate of the discretionary component of firm i’s accrual quality in year t, DiscAQi,t = l^i,t.

research_interest_evidence.quote: We focus on the component of information risk related to managers’ discretionary accounting choices and test whether the pricing of the discretionary component of information risk (hereafter, discretionary information risk) increases after restatements.
We use two approaches to test whether the factor loading on the DiscIR factor increases after a restatement.
The results, presented in Table 3, show that the increase in the discretionary information risk factor loading is 0.95, significant at the 1% level.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: The monthly DiscIR loading change is the focal H1 test of increased discretionary information-risk pricing.

review_notes: The principal question is whether restatements increase the pricing of discretionary information risk. Section 3.3 explicitly gives two approaches to that question: firm-specific event-time Eq. (1)/Table 2 and monthly cross-sectional Eq. (2)/Table 3; retain both as the paper’s paired H1 tests. The CAR association in Eq. (3)/Table 5, restatement-characteristic interactions in Eq. (4)/Table 6, the non-restatement industry-peer test, and the cost-of-capital arithmetic are later applications or follow-up questions, not part of the selected principal family.

The two retained factor-loading models require AQ factor construction. Eq. (5) generates residuals used to form AQ; Eq. (6) partitions AQ into DiscAQ residuals and InnateAQ fitted values. The supplied verified mathematical tails resolve the Eq. (1) event-month boundary, Eq. (5) lag, and fiscal-year t+1 portfolio timing. Eq. (5) and Eq. (6) estimator names are not stated; the exact TCA item calculation and Eq. (6) log bases are also not reported.
results_review_notes: Only the two frozen H1 baseline specifications are reported: the firm-specific event-time Eq. (1)/Table 2 model and the monthly cross-sectional Eq. (2)/Table 3 model. Later CAR, duration, restatement-characteristic, and cost-of-capital tests are excluded.

Table 2 reports mean firm-level OLS coefficients from 299 firm regressions, each estimated over 73 monthly event-time observations. Table 3 reports pre/post means and differences across 36 and 37 monthly cross-sectional coefficient estimates, respectively; each monthly cross-section uses the 299 restatement firms.
No regression-level standard errors or exact p-values are printed. The tables provide t-statistics and significance markers; unknown t degrees of freedom are left unspecified.

Table 4 monthly risk-factor premiums are retained only as raw factor-input summaries for retained model variables. Cost-of-capital rows and annualized values are excluded. Its printed size-factor label is SML, while the regressions label the factor SMB; that mapping remains unclear.
